Frequently asked questions

Short answers to common questions. For step-by-step instructions, see the guide.

Is Chord Transposer free?
Yes. It is free to use, with no sign-up or account.
Are my files uploaded to a server?
No. Chord charts you open or type are processed only in your browser and never leave your device. When you open a PDF or an image, the app downloads its reading libraries from a CDN, but your file is not sent.
Which files can I open?
Text files (including ChordPro files such as .cho and .crd), PDFs, and images such as PNG and JPEG. PDFs with text are read directly; scanned pages and images are read with OCR (Japanese and English). Up to the first 20 pages of a PDF are read. See opening files.
The text from my photo or scanned PDF is wrong. What can I do?
OCR can misread characters, especially in photos taken at an angle, in poor light, or at low resolution. Fix mistakes directly in Input — Output updates immediately. For better results, see the tips for photos and scanned PDFs. Handwritten charts are usually not recognized.
Why were some chords not transposed?
The app only changes text that looks like a chord. A single capital letter inside lyrics, such as "A" in "A man walked in", is left alone on purpose, and unusual symbols may not be recognized. ChordPro directives such as {key: G} are also not changed. Edit these in Input or by hand.
The chords no longer line up with the lyrics.
Chord charts line up only in a fixed-width (monospace) font, where every character has the same width. If you paste the result into a word processor, choose a font such as Courier New, Consolas, or MS Gothic. In Japanese lyrics, a full-width character takes the space of two half-width characters.
Why do I get A# when I expected Bb?
Both names are the same note. Set #/♭ to Prefer b for flat keys (F, Bb, Eb, Ab, Db, Gb) or Prefer # for sharp keys. See sharps or flats?.
How many semitones should I transpose?
Count the semitones from the old key to the new key, or look them up in the key-to-key table. For singing, try 1 or 2 semitones first. A karaoke key setting of +2 is the same as +2 in the app.
How do I rewrite a chart for playing with a capo?
Transpose by minus the capo fret. For capo 2, choose −2: the output shows the chord shapes to play. The capo chart shows which fret to use for each key.
Can I transpose minor keys and songs with key changes?
Yes. Every chord moves by the same number of semitones, so minor keys and key changes within a song keep their relationships.
Does it understand German H notation?
Yes. H is read as B (and Hm as Bm). Transposed chords are written with B.
Does it work on iPhone and Android?
Yes. It works in the browser on phones, tablets, and computers. On a phone, Input and Output are shown as tabs. You can also add it to your home screen; see install the app.
Can I use it offline?
Yes. After your first visit, the app opens and transposes without a connection. Opening PDFs and images needs a connection the first time, to download the reading libraries.
How do I print the result?
Open the preview. On a computer, use your browser's print command (Ctrl+P or ⌘P) in the preview window. On phones and tablets, tap the printer button; on iPhone and iPad, choose Print in the share menu. See preview, print, and save.
Is my chart saved?
The chart you are working on and your settings are kept in your browser so you can continue next time. They are not sent anywhere. To keep a copy, save it as a text file. To remove the stored data, clear this site's data in your browser settings.
How do I report a problem or suggest a feature?
Please open an issue on GitHub. If a chart is converted incorrectly, include a short example of the text.
